## The Riemann solver framework and the face-local frame {#sec-ch04-riemann}

### Summary

::: {.callout-note title="At a glance"}
- Takes the two face states of a direction and returns one flux per face.
- Switches: `dynamics/riemann-solver/{type,dir}`; YAML defaults `roe` and `omni`.
- Six types are registered: `roe`, `lmars`, `hllc`, `upwind`, `shallow-roe`, `plume-roe`.
- The momentum rows are rotated into a face-local frame by an index map, not by a matrix.
- Only some solvers can return a face pressure; the base class refuses the request outright.
:::

Every face carries one flux, and the solver's job is to produce it from the two one-sided states the
reconstruction left there. Which solver is chosen changes the numbers but not the structure of the operator:
the divergence of @sec-ch04-divergence consumes the result the same way whatever produced it.

### Derivation

The physical flux through a face depends only on the component of velocity normal to it and on the two
tangential components as passive quantities. Rather than rotate the state with a matrix, the code renames the
rows: for direction `dim` the normal momentum row is

$$
\mathrm{ivx} = \mathrm{IPR} - \mathrm{dim},
$$ {#eq-ch04-riemann-frame}

and the two tangential rows follow by cycling. `[C8]` checks that this is a permutation of the three momentum
rows for each of the three directions, which is what makes a single solver body correct for all of them. The
cost is that the row index of "the normal velocity" is not fixed, and reading any solver body requires holding
@eq-ch04-riemann-frame in mind.

The rotation is only the labelling. On a curved grid the face-local frame is also a genuine change of basis,
and that projection is done by the coordinate object before the solver is called, not inside it.

### Numerical method

```{python}
#| label: fig-ch04-riemann-face
#| fig-cap: "One face and what the solver sees. The reconstruction leaves a left state (green) and a right state (blue) on the two sides of the face (thick orange line); the solver returns a single face velocity and face pressure (orange) from which the flux of every row is built. The arrow labelled n is the face normal, and the normal momentum row is selected by the index map rather than by a rotation matrix."
#| fig-alt: "Two adjacent cells separated by a thick vertical line, with an arrow pointing right from the left cell labelled w L, an arrow pointing left from the right cell labelled w R, a normal direction arrow, and a label for the face velocity and pressure."
#| echo: false
from snapy_report.ch04.fig_riemann_face import make_fig
make_fig()
```

The factory is `create` ([`riemann_solver.cpp:50-71`](https://github.com/chengcli/snapy/blob/e894700ff7aee30b52882e5202b16461413780b0/src/riemann/riemann_solver.cpp#L50-L71)) and the option parsing
[`riemann_solver.cpp:23-31`](https://github.com/chengcli/snapy/blob/e894700ff7aee30b52882e5202b16461413780b0/src/riemann/riemann_solver.cpp#L23-L31), where the default type is `roe` and the default direction scope is
`omni`. Note that the default is `roe` and not the `lmars` that the example decks select: a deck that omits
the key does not get the production solver.

The base class `forward` at [`riemann_solver.cpp:39-48`](https://github.com/chengcli/snapy/blob/e894700ff7aee30b52882e5202b16461413780b0/src/riemann/riemann_solver.cpp#L39-L48) is the `upwind` solver, and it is also the
place where the face-pressure contract is enforced: it fails outright if a caller asks it for a face pressure.
That matters because the well-balanced $x_1$ path of @sec-ch05 and the geometric source of @sec-ch04-sphsrc
both need a face pressure, so choosing a solver that cannot produce one silently changes which pressure force
the $x_1$ momentum row sees. Of the six types, `lmars`, `hllc` and `roe` write one.

Each solver is declared in `LmarsSolverImpl` ([`riemann_solver.hpp:79-207`](https://github.com/chengcli/snapy/blob/e894700ff7aee30b52882e5202b16461413780b0/src/riemann/riemann_solver.hpp#L79-L207)) as a thin module wrapping a dispatch call,
and the numerics live in a header shared between the CPU and CUDA paths.

### Limits

::: {.callout-warning title="Limits"}
- The YAML default solver is `roe`, not the `lmars` the shipped decks use. Omitting the key changes the scheme.
- Three of the six types cannot return a face pressure. Selecting one of those changes the $x_1$ pressure force
  on a curved grid and in the well-balanced path, and the only signal is a hard failure if something asks.
:::

1. **`dir` is parsed and its effect is not documented.** The key is read into the options and no source in the
   repository explains what scope `omni` selects against the alternatives.
